recent_candidates.title: Elections pose next test for Venezuela
recent_candidates.author: Shelby Talcott
recent_candidates.excerpt: Venezuela’s next big test will be whether it can turn the Trump administration’s plan for elections into a genuine transition to democratic rule. And with the US midterms over soon, the issue will soon face renewed interest from Washington. Interim Venezuelan President Delcy Rodríguez held a rare address last week in which she vowed to hold elections — an ambitious promise for a government still navigating political upheaval following the US’ arrest of President Nicolás Maduro in January. But no election date has been set, as opposition leader María Corina Machado emphasized in her own remarks shortly afterwards. Meanwhile, Rodríguez is already signaling an interest in working with Washington, despite some of her public rhetoric, tapping former opposition aide Oliver Blanco as foreign minister. — Shelby Talcott

recent_candidates.title: Election ‘war rooms’ enter the AI age
recent_candidates.author: Ashley Gold
recent_candidates.excerpt: Both OpenAI and Anthropic will have “war rooms” dedicated to ensuring their platforms provide accurate information about the midterm elections, a first for both companies. The concept of a tech platform “war room” dates back to 2018, when Meta stood one up for the first time amid concerns about the proliferation of election-related misinformation. The AI age has supercharged those threats, which now include deepfake videos and AI-powered search results spreading incorrect information. Case in point: Last week, Google’s AI Mode wouldn’t respond to a query about who won the 2020 election, which the company said they were working to fix . “Teams across the company work year-round on strengthening our election-related safeguards and enforcing our policies. Ahead of the election, we have a dedicated war room monitoring our platform for misuse and ready to quickly respond to any incidents,” an Anthropic spokesperson told Semafor. These efforts will be made more difficult by AI’s unpredictable nature, recent cybersecurity issues, and the tendency of AI search tools to reflect back results users want to see. Former Meta director of public policy Katie Harbath told Semafor that war rooms are “built for dealing with the things we can’t necessarily predict going wrong and you need a quick, established process in terms of triaging.”

recent_candidates.title: New creator brand Magnet Originals launches
recent_candidates.author: Max Tani
recent_candidates.excerpt: Megan Cunningham, an advertising industry veteran and founder of Magnet Media, is on Monday launching Magnet Originals, a brand to help established personalities grow their media empires and to incubate the next generation of stars. Former TikTok executive Dustin Goot and former Vice exec Subrata De are both joining in senior roles, alongside media operators Alexandra Zaslow and Brannan Goetschius. Magnet Originals will provide advice and production support for media personalities, including Justin Tranter, Boyz II Men’s Shawn Stockman, and former NBA star Byron Scott. It will also build on its own original franchises. The company said it is launching with a docuseries from the poet and critic Hanif Abdurraqib and a music show hosted by Billboard executive editor Lyndsey Havens, both co-produced with Live Nation, as well as , a show co-hosted by comedian Sam Jay, Olympic gymnast Jordan Chiles, and broadcaster Ari Chambers. The company is also hoping to build a business around training the next generation of creators. Its Top Creator Academy will offer courses and one-on-one consulting with professionals. Cunningham told Semafor that she saw the program growing into a seven-figure business on its own. “Documentaries can’t count on distribution, and newsrooms keep closing because their business model is in jeopardy. … I was watching a generation of entrepreneurial, brilliant storytellers build podcasts, YouTube channels, and newsletters on sweat equity alone,” Cunningham said.

recent_candidates.author: Nicholas Wu
recent_candidates.excerpt: The News Democratic party leaders have found themselves unable to stave off an embarrassing schism in Michigan’s must-win Senate race, a crisis that may offer a glimpse of internal battles to come. Haley Stevens culminated in Stevens’ surprise Sunday endorsement of Republican nominee Mike Rogers. Stevens appeared with Rogers at a Black church in Detroit less than 24 hours after vowing to colleagues that she would back El-Sayed, winning praise from President Donald Trump and calls for her eviction from the House Democratic Caucus. But perhaps the most stunning aspect of the crackup was how hard senior Democrats had worked to avoid it. Party leaders like Reps. recent_candidates.excerpt: The FBI said that North Korea was responsible for stealing $6.3 billion from Binance last week in the largest-ever crypto heist , dealing a blow to the sector’s dream of becoming a mainstream asset. recent_candidates.title: US approves sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine
recent_candidates.author: Lauren Morganbesser
recent_candidates.excerpt: US approval of the sale of 500 Patriot interceptors to Ukraine offers little immediate relief, analysts said, as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that deliveries could take “a few years.” The $2.1 billion sale — funded through donations from Canada, Germany, and Norway — underscores Washington’s shift to relying on allies to cover the costs of Ukraine’s military assistance. As global interceptor stockpiles dwindle and Russian attacks intensify, Zelenskyy urged the US and Europe to provide interceptors “ now ” rather than wait for new production. But Washington’s own military priorities may constrain supplies: “Perhaps they intend to restart the war in Iran and don’t know how many Patriot missiles they’re going to need for themselves ,” a former American ambassador to NATO told Euronews. — Lauren Morganbesser

La Liga’s president has met with China’s ambassador to Spain to help “ find solutions .” — Brendan Ruberry

recent_candidates.title: Democrats eye state supreme court races — this year and beyond
recent_candidates.author: By Casey He
recent_candidates.excerpt: Liberal groups have spent millions in a handful of battleground state supreme court races ahead of Tuesday’s elections, looking to lay the groundwork for Democrats to win control of more courts ahead of a crucial redistricting cycle. At the center of the fight are races for Republican-majority state supreme courts in North Carolina and Ohio, where this year’s results could set the stage for Democrats to flip the makeup of the benches in 2028. National groups are also spending to defend the liberal majority on Michigan’s court and on an open seat in Montana, where voters will also decide whether judicial elections remain nonpartisan. The investments are yet another reflection of how state supreme court elections have become national political battlegrounds. The high court justices have become arbiters of major disputes, from abortion rights to election integrity and redistricting. Those who win in the coming cycles will likely preside over challenges to congressional and legislative maps that are drawn in a handful of states after the midterm election — and then nationwide after the 2030 census . Nowhere are the contests more heated than in North Carolina. recent_candidates.title: The size of Democrats’ victory Tuesday could help determine their future
recent_candidates.author: By Erin Doherty, Jason Beeferman, Lisa Kashinsky and Lauren Fedor
recent_candidates.excerpt: For Democrats, the size of their victory matters. Progressives and moderates have been sparring all cycle over who will get to claim credit if they win on Tuesday. A new POLITICO Poll shows that the bigger the win, the more Democrats appear inclined to see it as a mandate to run more progressive candidates. A smaller-than-expected victory next week would leave the party — and voters — torn over which direction to go. The results reveal that the midterm election will have major implications over the next stage of the Democratic Party war over their identity — and could give progressives fresh ammunition ahead of a critical 2028 presidential race. Party insiders are closely watching contests where that infighting has been on display: From Abdul El-Sayed’s battle for Michigan Senate and Troy Jackson’s for Maine Senate, to Randy Villegas’ House race in California and Manny Rutinel’s in Colorado. More than a dozen Democratic Party operatives and strategists said in interviews that both factions are already preparing to see a blue wave as validation of its own approach. Top super PACs and campaign firms are finishing strategy memos and finalizing lineups for a slate of post-election conferences where they intend to claim their way is the party’s future. “You know what they say: Victory has a thousand mothers, right?” said Oliver Libby, the Democratic author behind the book “Strong Floor, No Ceiling,” which became a rallying cry for House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries this cycle.

The summer after her freshman year of college, she got a job as a backpacking guide in Colorado, planning and leading camping trips in the Rocky Mountains. Ath noticed that the people she encountered in that environment tended to be secular and politically progressive. The experience made her wonder if there was a place for people like herself, a conservative Catholic who was passionate about the outdoors. Now, a decade later, this mother of four is cofounder of the new nonprofit Vita Et Terra, which is part of a growing conservative environmental movement that sees more humans as a solution, not a problem. recent_candidates.title: Bulgaria set to elect its first female president as Russia-friendly Iliana Yotova wins runoff
recent_candidates.excerpt: Bulgaria’s acting president, Iliana Yotova, won the second round of the country’s presidential election on November 1. With 99.68% of ballots counted, preliminary results showed 57.6% of voters had voted for Yotova and 39.3% for her main rival, former interim Prime Minister Andrey Gyurov. Gyurov conceded defeat. Yotova has twice served as Bulgaria’s vice president under President Rumen Radev. Radev stepped down early in January 2026 to run in parliamentary elections, and Yotova temporarily took over as president. If the results are confirmed, Yotova will become the first woman elected president in Bulgaria’s history. In the first round, neither candidate received the votes needed to win outright. Yotova took 34.76% of the vote, while Gyurov took 31.94%. Turnout was extremely low in both rounds: 23% in the first round and 27% in the second. Prime Minister Rumen Radev’s Progressive Bulgaria party, which won an absolute majority in April’s parliamentary elections, backed Yotova’s candidacy. According to AP, Yotova’s victory will allow Radev’s ruling majority to retain control of the presidency. Like Radev, Yotova supports negotiations with Russia and a diplomatic settlement to the war in Ukraine. She also opposes providing military aid to Kyiv and supports lifting sanctions on Russia. Michigan’s decision to skip letter grades for incoming freshmen has added fuel to the fire. Students can get into elite universities, and graduate, still lacking basic skills. How did we end up here? Of course, administrators do want high retention and good graduation rates, including on-time graduation. recent_candidates.excerpt: Ante una tragedia como el accidente de trenes de Toledo, en la que numerosas personas se han visto afectadas y muchas familias afrontan momentos de enorme dolor, saber cómo actuar y qué decir resulta fundamental. Acompañar a una persona que acaba de perder a un ser querido no siempre es sencillo. A veces, las palabras no son suficientes y un gesto de cariño puede convertirse en el apoyo más necesario.
